mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a three-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in industrial production exceeding 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month change < -1.0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% over a six-month window signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 1% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST) signals a demand shift from durable goods to services, which benefits technology and service sector stocks and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% while HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for six consecutive months in a late-cycle environment signals labor market tightness, which raises wage inflation and input costs, compressing margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% for six consecutive months and decision_date_used after 2010-01-01
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered late-cycle episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above trend for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.
